text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000561 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, but with only three documented 99215 claims the records are too thin to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not just a panel effect. The by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running roughly double the all-provider share at every condition count, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. The low-complexity sample includes visits billed at the highest level for routine-looking diagnoses, such as follow-up only (C0296313, C0296452, C0297414) and upper respiratory infection (C0296588). That pattern is consistent with upcoding. Against this, the 99215 claims sampled on older patients with four or five conditions (e.g., C0297230, C0298197) look plausible. The three documented 99215 claims (C0296765, C0297834, C0298380) all recorded high MDM, and only one documented claim overall (C0297330, a 99214) fell below its billed level. However, records cover a very small share of claims, and the 3 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed without a lab or test line on the claim are a weak signal of possible cloned or inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, starting with the follow-up and acute minor-illness visits, to see whether documented MDM or time supports the level billed."}
